_comment: The misconceptions Cambridge names for Stage 3, from the 'Common misconceptions' table in each of the 25 topics of the Teacher's Resource 3. Ids are `<topic>-m<N>`. The Stage 3 pack has no Ready to Go Lessons, so unlike Stage 2 there is no second source and no rtg-NN ids; the Workbook 3 carries exercises rather than misconceptions, and the Teacher's Guide 3 PDF has no text layer at all (153 pages of images), so nothing could be read from it. 46 rows were printed across the 25 tables; see _excluded for the three that are not here.
source: Cambridge Primary Science Teacher's Resource 3 (Board & Cross), Common misconceptions, topics 1.1-6.3
_minimumCovered: Raised to the measured value when the depth pass lands; coverage is a number that only goes up.

_excluded._comment: Printed in a Stage 3 table and deliberately NOT in this fixture. The first is Cambridge deferring itself; the other two are the same row twice.
_excluded.liquid particles as well as small pieces: Teacher's Resource 3, topic 2.4: 'The concept that matter is made up of particles is not introduced in the curriculum until Stage 4.' Answering it here would teach past the stage - the filtering row that IS here (2.4-m1) needs no particles.
duplicate rows folded into one entry: 3.1 lists 'my shadow is attached to me' as its second AND its fourth row, with different How to identify / How to overcome text -> one entry, 3.1-m2
1.4 lists 'the more they water a plant the healthier it will be' and 'some learners overestimate the amount of water needed' as two rows of one idea -> one entry, 1.4-m1

misconceptions.misconception: A river or a flame is living, because it moves and changes.
misconceptions.overcome: Moving is only one of the seven things a living thing does. A flame does not feed, grow from a young one, sense things or make young. Check all seven, not just one.

misconceptions.misconception: All leaves and all plants are green.
misconceptions.overcome: Many plants have red, purple or silver leaves, and they are plants just the same. Green is the commonest colour, not a rule.

misconceptions.misconception: Seaweed and mushrooms are plants.
misconceptions.overcome: They look a little like plants, but they have none of the parts a plant has - no roots, no stem, no leaves, no flower - so scientists do not count them as plants.

misconceptions.misconception: A flower and a plant are the same thing - 'flower' is another word for 'plant'.
misconceptions.overcome: A flower is one PART of a plant, the part where seeds are made. The plant also has roots, a stem and leaves.

misconceptions.misconception: Flowers are there to be pretty for people.
misconceptions.overcome: A flower's job is making seeds, so new plants can grow. People liking them is a lucky extra.

misconceptions.misconception: A plant makes its food all the time, day and night.
misconceptions.overcome: A leaf needs light to make food, so it makes food in the daytime and stops in the dark.

misconceptions.misconception: The Moon gives plants light to make food at night.
misconceptions.overcome: Moonlight is only weak sunlight bounced back, far too weak to make food - and on some nights there is no moonlight at all.

misconceptions.topicTitle: Plants need water and the right temperature
misconceptions.misconception: The more you water a plant, the healthier it will be.
misconceptions.overcome: It does not rain every day, and most plants are fine for a day or two between waterings. Most water you pour on sinks away through the soil. Plants want damp soil, not wet soil.

misconceptions.misconception: Sugar, flour and rice are liquids, because they pour and take the shape of the pot.
misconceptions.overcome: Look at one grain through a magnifying glass: it keeps its own shape. A heap of tiny solid pieces pours, and every piece is still a solid.

misconceptions.misconception: All gas is dangerous.
misconceptions.overcome: 'Gas' is the word for the one that burns in a cooker, and also for oxygen, which you are breathing right now. Some gases are dangerous and some keep you alive.

misconceptions.misconception: A funnel or a measuring cylinder will separate a mixture.
misconceptions.overcome: A funnel only guides things into a narrow neck and a cylinder only measures. To separate you need something that holds one material back: a sieve, a filter or a magnet.

misconceptions.misconception: When a solid dissolves it has gone.
misconceptions.overcome: It is still there, spread out too small to see. Taste tells you the sugar is in the water, and letting the water dry leaves the sugar behind.

misconceptions.misconception: A filter will take dissolved salt or sugar out of water.
misconceptions.overcome: Filter salty water and the water that comes through is still salty. Let it dry and the salt is there. A filter catches pieces you can see, not what has dissolved.

misconceptions.misconception: Water that looks clean is safe to drink.
misconceptions.overcome: Tiny living things too small to see can live in water that looks perfectly clear, and some of them make people ill. Only drink water a grown-up says is safe.

misconceptions.misconception: Leather and wool do not come from planet Earth, because they come from animals.
misconceptions.overcome: The animal ate plants, and the plant made its food from water, air and sunlight. Follow it back and every animal material starts with the Earth.

misconceptions.misconception: The air is not part of planet Earth.
misconceptions.overcome: The air is a layer of gases wrapped round the Earth and held on by its gravity. It is as much part of the planet as the rock.

misconceptions.misconception: A shadow shows the colours and the details of the thing, like a photograph.
misconceptions.overcome: A shadow is one flat dark shape with no colour and no detail, because it is simply where the light could not reach.

misconceptions.misconception: My shadow is joined to my feet.
misconceptions.overcome: Jump, and the shadow stays on the ground. Lift an object off the floor and its shadow stays down there too. Nothing is joined to anything.

misconceptions.misconception: You always have a shadow; the Sun only lights it up so you can see it.
misconceptions.overcome: Stand where no light reaches you and there is no shadow at all. A shadow is made by a light, not shown up by one.

misconceptions.misconception: A thing's shadow is always the shape you are used to seeing it.
misconceptions.overcome: Turn a cup and its shadow changes from a circle to a rectangle. The shadow is the shape of the thing as the light meets it.

misconceptions.misconception: A coloured material cannot be transparent.
misconceptions.overcome: Coloured glass and sunglasses let light through and you can see through them. They colour the light rather than stopping it.

misconceptions.misconception: Water is not a material, so it cannot be transparent.
misconceptions.overcome: Water is a material, and clean water is transparent - you can read through a glass of it. Dirty water is not, which shows the difference is in the water.

misconceptions.misconception: Translucent means glowing, or very shiny.
misconceptions.overcome: Translucent means light gets through but scatters, so you see a glow and not a clear picture. Tracing paper and frosted glass are translucent and neither glows.

misconceptions.misconception: The stomach is the whole lower part of your body.
misconceptions.overcome: The stomach is one organ, a bag just below the heart. Most of the room lower down is taken by the intestines.

misconceptions.misconception: A lung is just an empty bag of air.
misconceptions.overcome: A lung is spongy, full of tiny spaces, and packed with blood vessels. That is how the oxygen gets from the air into your blood.

misconceptions.topicTitle: Animal groups and different life cycles
misconceptions.misconception: A caterpillar and a butterfly are two different animals.
misconceptions.overcome: They are one animal at two stages of its life, like a tadpole and a frog. Some animals change shape completely as they grow.

misconceptions.topicTitle: Animal groups and different life cycles
misconceptions.misconception: A spider is an insect.
misconceptions.overcome: Count the legs: an insect has six and a spider has eight. Spiders are in their own group, the arachnids.

misconceptions.misconception: The arrows in a food chain point from the animal to the thing it eats.
misconceptions.overcome: The arrow shows which way the food and its energy travel, so it points from the thing eaten TO the eater: plant to mouse, mouse to cat.

misconceptions.misconception: Animals get their energy by sleeping.
misconceptions.overcome: Sleep rests you, and it gives you no energy. Energy comes from food: a plant gets it from sunlight, an animal by eating another living thing.

misconceptions.misconception: Fossils are only a few years old.
misconceptions.overcome: The animals in fossils are nothing like the ones alive now, and they were buried for millions of years.

misconceptions.misconception: The fossil IS the animal.
misconceptions.overcome: A fossil is a shape left in rock - a print of part of the animal. Press a shell into clay and lift it out: the shape is not the shell.

misconceptions.misconception: All fossils are fake.
misconceptions.overcome: A few fakes have been made, and there are many thousands of real fossils in museums that tell us what used to live here.

misconceptions.misconception: Whether a thing moves depends on its shape - a ball moves because it is round.
misconceptions.overcome: Put a ball and a book on a table and neither moves. Both need a push. The round shape only means the ball keeps going for longer once it has been pushed.

misconceptions.misconception: Moving things slow down by themselves.
misconceptions.overcome: Something always pushes back. A bicycle slows because the brakes push on the wheels, and a rolling ball slows because the air and the ground push against it.

misconceptions.misconception: Weight is measured in grams and kilograms.
misconceptions.overcome: Grams and kilograms measure MASS, how much material a thing is made of. Weight is the pull of gravity on it, and a forcemeter measures it in newtons.

misconceptions.misconception: Heavy things fall faster than light things.
misconceptions.overcome: Drop a marble and a book together and they land together. A leaf falls slowly only because it has to push so much air out of the way, not because gravity pulls it less.

misconceptions.misconception: There is no friction in water.
misconceptions.overcome: Slightly wet coins slide LESS easily than dry ones. A lot of water can cut friction down, but a little water increases it.

misconceptions.misconception: A round magnet has only one pole.
misconceptions.overcome: Every magnet has two. Bring a labelled bar magnet up to a round one and you can find the north end and the south end on it.

misconceptions.misconception: All metals are magnetic.
misconceptions.overcome: Only a few are - iron, steel, nickel and cobalt. Test an aluminium can, a copper coin and a gold ring and the magnet ignores all three.

misconceptions.topicTitle: The shape of the Earth, Sun and Moon
misconceptions.misconception: The Sun and the Moon are the same size, because they look the same size.
misconceptions.overcome: The Sun is more than a hundred times wider than the Earth and the Moon is a quarter of the Earth's width. The Sun only looks small because it is so very far away.

misconceptions.topicTitle: The shape of the Earth, Sun and Moon
misconceptions.misconception: There is no gravity on the Moon, so an astronaut would float away.
misconceptions.overcome: Astronauts walk and jump on the Moon and come back down. The Moon's gravity is weaker than the Earth's, so they fall more slowly - not not at all.

misconceptions.misconception: The Moon only comes up at night.
misconceptions.overcome: The Moon is often in the sky in the daytime. It is simply much harder to spot against a bright blue sky.

misconceptions.misconception: The Moon changes shape.
misconceptions.overcome: The Moon is always a ball. We see the lit part, and how much of it we can see changes. In a daytime crescent you can often make out the dark part too.
